assessment.title: Immigration Pathway Assessment
assessment.subtitle: Find Your Best Path Forward
assessment.description: Answer a few questions to discover which immigration pathways might be right for you.
assessment.question1: What is your primary immigration goal?
assessment.question2: Do you have family members who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents?
assessment.question3: Do you have a job offer or employment opportunity in the U.S.?
assessment.question4: How long have you been in the United States?
assessment.resultsDescription: Based on your answers, here are the immigration pathways that may be suitable for you:

family.title: Family-Based Immigration
family.subtitle: Reunite with Your Loved Ones
family.description: Family-based immigration allows U.S. citizens and permanent residents to sponsor certain family members for immigration to the United States.
family.eligibility1: U.S. Citizens can sponsor: spouses, children, parents, and siblings
family.eligibility2: Permanent Residents can sponsor: spouses and unmarried children
family.step3: Apply for immigrant visa or adjustment of status
family.timelineText: Processing times vary from several months to several years depending on the relationship and country of origin.

employment.title: Employment-Based Immigration
employment.subtitle: Work and Build Your Career in the U.S.
employment.description: Employment-based immigration provides pathways for foreign workers with specific skills, education, or job offers to work and live in the United States.
employment.eb1: EB-1: Priority workers (extraordinary ability, outstanding professors/researchers, multinational executives)
employment.eb2: EB-2: Advanced degree professionals or exceptional ability
employment.eb3: EB-3: Skilled workers, professionals, other workers
employment.step4: Apply for adjustment of status or immigrant visa

citizenship.title: Citizenship & Naturalization
citizenship.subtitle: Become a U.S. Citizen
citizenship.description: Naturalization is the process by which lawful permanent residents become U.S. citizens, gaining the right to vote and full participation in American civic life.
citizenship.req2: Be a permanent resident for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen)
citizenship.req3: Demonstrate continuous residence and physical presence
